chunks: And with this chain, from Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: I heard him saying:

He was asked about marriage in the month of Shawwal, so he said: 'Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) married Aisha in Shawwal, and he said: 'It was only the people of the early times who disliked that in Shawwal, and that is because the plague struck them, so the virgins and the brides-to-be perished, so they disliked it for that reason, not for any other reason.'

key_terms.الْمُمْلَكَات: Brides-to-be (women whose dowry has been paid or who are betrothed)
key_terms.شَوَّال: Shawwal (the tenth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)

ai.seo_question: Why did early Muslims dislike marriage in Shawwal and is it forbidden?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the aversion to marriage in Shawwal is merely cultural (urf), not a religious prohibition (hukm), by citing the Prophet’s own marriage to Aisha in that month. He attributes this cultural dislike to a historical plague that decimated young women (virgins and brides) during the early Islamic era, leading people to avoid weddings in that month out of superstition rather than divine command.
